packages.title: Public BUB1B splice map on Kaggle (Pangolin, every possible SNV)
packages.progress: Ran on the private Kaggle notebook santanubanerjee9/bub1b-splice-map, pushed by an idle-slot waiter at 00:30 IST: 180,165 SNVs in 62 min on 2x T4. Checks: matched Pangolin's compute_score to 5e-5 (fp32) and 2e-4 (fp16); all 7 published controls as expected. Output in D:\mva-hackathon\refs\bub1b\kaggle_out; local lookup with pipeline/splice_map.py. Finding: 75 intronic SNVs (0.04%) would create a strong cryptic site at 15 nt or more from canonical sites; the published cryptic-acceptor alleles sit 4-10 nt away, so up-regulation is the more plausible antisense route for BUB1B.
packages.done_when: A private Kaggle notebook scores every possible SNV across the BUB1B gene with Pangolin (GPL-3.0). The worksheet gains a summary of where antisense-correctable cryptic sites could arise. No patient data is involved.

packages.title: Wire gnomAD v4.1 frequencies into the annotation table
packages.done_when: refs/gnomad/manifest.json shows no failures and compressed_and_indexed: true. If not, rerun `python tools/fetch_gnomad_slices.py`: every finished query is cached, so a rerun fetches only what is missing and then compresses. Run it when the laptop is quiet; it runs at idle priority. Then annotate_vcf.sh adds AF_joint, nhomalt_joint and fafmax_faf95_max_joint from the slices, matching on chrom, pos, ref and alt after norm, with the slices' chr contigs mapped to the VCF's no-chr names. annotate_table.py takes pop_af from gnomAD where the variant is covered and falls back to ClinVar's ExAC/1000G/ESP maximum elsewhere. It records a pop_af_source column (gnomad_v4.1, clinvar or none), and records inside a covered region but absent from gnomAD count as AF 0, not unknown. comphet/track1_rank use fafmax_faf95_max_joint for rarity, with thresholds stated in methods §B3. Synthetic tests cover a gnomAD-common variant being dropped, an absent covered variant being rare, and an uncovered variant falling back. All tests pass. Public data only: never look up the child's variants online.
